transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Because water is on the floor right next to your plug sockets, this is an immediate electrical hazard. Please do not touch the sockets or switch anything on until a qualified electrician or engineer has checked that it is safe to do so. Regarding the leak itself, common causes are a blocked filter causing overflow, something caught in the door seal letting water escape, or a spray arm being blocked by tall dishes and spraying water out of the door.
its still running tho and theres loads of bubbles coming out the door. the water is spreading towards an extension lead on the floor, what do i do?? i dont know where the fuse box is

This is a serious emergency because water is touching your extension lead, which could cause an electric shock or fire. Please do not touch the plug, socket, or extension lead. If you can find your fuse box (usually in a hallway, cupboard, or near the meter), switch off the main switch or the kitchen circuit immediately. If you cannot find it or are unsure, call the electricity emergency service on 0800 40 50 60 right now. The bubbles suggest you may have used the wrong detergent (like washing-up liquid) which creates foam that escapes the door. However, because of the electrical danger, do not try to fix this yourself until a qualified electrician or engineer has confirmed it is safe.
i dont know where the fuse box is and its my landlords machine. can i just turn the dishwasher off at the button? the water is nearly at the extension lead

No, do not press any buttons on the dishwasher. Because water is spreading towards your extension lead, touching the machine or its controls could give you an electric shock if electricity is present in the water. You must switch off the power at the main fuse box immediately. If you cannot find it, call the Electricity Emergency Service on 0800 40 50 60 right now. Once the power is safely cut and a qualified electrician has confirmed it is safe to proceed, we can look into why this happened. The bubbles suggest you may have used washing-up liquid or too much detergent, which creates foam that escapes the door. However, because of the electrical hazard, do not attempt any checks until an engineer has verified safety.
i still dont know where the fuse box is?? theres a socket on the wall by it and the water is nearly at the extension lead. should i just ring that number

Yes, please ring 0800 40 50 60 right now. Since you don't know where your fuse box is and water is nearly touching an extension lead, this is a life-threatening electrical hazard that only the electricity emergency service can safely resolve by isolating the power at their end or sending an engineer immediately. Once the power is confirmed off and it is safe to approach the machine, you will need a qualified appliance engineer to fix the leak. The bubbles suggest you may have used washing-up liquid instead of dishwasher detergent, which creates foam that overflows from the door.

Blocked filter or sump causing overflow (medium)
